content.comment_body: Hello, I'm experiencing an issue with my [product_name] operator device. I created a diagram that displays text, and everything works fine during simulation. However, after downloading the project, the [product_name] operator device does not show the text. I've double-checked that all priority pages are enabled, and I am sending the appropriate signaling text to all text blocks. The colored markers and logic both function correctly; pressing F1-F4 buttons in online simulation works as expected. On the actual device, only the date and time display, and I am able to access the settings and DI/DO page. Can anyone advise why the texts appear in simulation but not on the real device? I hope my explanation is clear. Thank you.
It's difficult to diagnose without seeing your program. Please upload your project as a ZIP file so it can be reviewed and troubleshooting advice can be given.

Apologies, I have attached the file right away. Note: If anyone downloads this to a [product_name] and receives an error regarding maximum space reached, this refers to the diagram layout space; the core logic will still be loaded and operational. SOFTWARE VERSION: [product_name] SC [version_no]. Thanks again for your assistance.

The program appears to be corrupted. I cannot determine the exact cause. When exporting the program and changing hardware to [article_no] standard, then saving and trying to open it with [product_name] SC [version_no], it cancels with an error. Transferring the original program to my [product_name] shows in the status that message texts are active, but nothing is displayed on my [product_name] operator device. However, changing the device's background color works. I recommend submitting a support request and having [company_name] review your program.

After debugging and copying parts of the diagram, I discovered that logic in page 15, block [article_no], was stopping the signaling system. By adjusting that logic, everything now works as intended. Thank you for your support.

analysis.insight_summary: Users faced a mismatch between simulated and real device behavior, where message texts programmed to show up on the [product_name] operator device appeared in simulation but not after deployment. Core functions and signaling, including color changes, operated correctly, making the issue harder to identify. Final diagnosis revealed a logic problem on a specific page blocked the signaling pathway to the device. This underscores the need for thorough debugging and better diagnostic tools for project deployment.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect that message texts tested successfully in simulation will display identically on the actual [product_name] operator device after deployment, and anticipate clear indication or diagnostics if device logic interferes with proper text display.
